newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end higher in active trading.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end higher in active trading.

text.p: Israeli shares closed broadly higher on increased turnover on Thursday after three days of profit-taking, dealers said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 1.57 percent, or 3.19 points, to 206.45 on all-share turnover of 92 million shekels against 72 million shekels on Wednesday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index gained 1.64 percent to 215.28.
"The market is positive and investors are very optimistic. After few days of profit-taking the market has resumed its positive momentum," said Danniella Finn, head of sales at Batucha Securities.
"The positive trend started on Wednesday towards the end of the trading day when the market recovered from early losses. Activity increased today and the market looks very good," Finn added.
"The decline we saw at the beginning of week was only a technical correction. I believe that the positive trend will continue next week," said Uri Schur at Eyal Securities.

The main gainer on the Maof was Clal Electronics Industries, which surged 4.75 percent to 30,173 after its Nasdaq-traded affiliate ECI Telecom rose 3.4 percent on very high volume of $20 million on Wednesday.

The most active shares were IDB Holdings, which rose 2.0 percent to 1,248 on volume of 6.1 million shekels; Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which lost 0.5 percent to 146,565 on volume of 5.9 million shekels; and Israel Chemicals, which gained 2.0 percent to 285 on turnover of 3.3 million shekels.
